chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Whoever pronounces three divorces in one sitting while not in a state of purity (during menstruation), this amounts to nothing. The only divorce is that which God, Mighty and Majestic, has commanded; so whoever violates this, there is no divorce for him.
And indeed Ibn Umar divorced his wife three times in one sitting while she was menstruating, and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) ordered him to take her back and not count the divorce.

He said: And a man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said, 'O Commander of the Faithful, I have divorced my wife.' He said: 'Do you have witnesses?' He said: 'No.' So he said: 'Be gone.'

key_terms.بَيِّنَة: Clear proof/witnesses — in Islamic law, typically two just witnesses required for the validity of legal acts
key_terms.طُهْر: Purity — specifically the inter-menstrual period when sexual intercourse is permissible and divorce may be validly pronounced
key_terms.مَجْلِس: Session/sitting — a single continuous meeting; triple divorce in one sitting is held invalid

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir say about triple divorce in one sitting according to Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) lays down the Shia jurisprudential ruling that a triple divorce pronounced in a single sitting — or during menstruation — is null and void, citing the precedent of Ibn Umar whose three-fold divorce during his wife's menstruation was invalidated by the Prophet (SAWW). This reflects a fundamental disagreement between Shia and Sunni law: Shia fiqh requires each divorce to be in a separate period of purity, with witnesses, otherwise the divorce is invalid. The second anecdote reinforces the requirement of two witnesses for any divorce to be legally valid, as Ali (AS) dismisses the man's claim without witnesses.
